seed: An SVG logo comes into a video and stays sharp at any size (video-title-wt.html, the Media shelf: 'svg, png, a logo. It keeps its own scale, so blowing one up on a 4K frame stays crisp'). File > Import Media takes an SVG onto the Library shelf, captioned with its name over its kind (Acme Logo / svg); a Finder drop on the shelf takes one too (Sparkle / svg); its tile let go on the timeline lands on a Gfx track over the recording; the same file dragged from the Finder onto the picture lands where it is let go, and one carried onto the timeline lands on a graphics track. Blown up next to the PNG of the same logo, the SVG keeps hard edges while the PNG goes soft. At Next defaults, no flag set.

steps.comment: File > Import Media (Shift Command I). The menu bar is frozen under a walk that is not in front, so the command is run directly.

steps.says: Acme Logo.svg is in the Library

steps.note: THE FIRST TEST: Import Media took an SVG. It is a tile on the Media shelf captioned Acme Logo over svg, the way the mock's art tiles read (Sparkle / svg), and nothing landed on the picture
THE SECOND TEST: the SVG tile let go over the recording landed on a new Gfx track from 0:02 for five seconds, like a PNG
THE THIRD TEST: the same SVG dragged from the Finder onto the picture landed where it was let go, at its own size, picked; the refusal note it used to show is gone
THE FOURTH TEST: the SVG (top) and the PNG of the same logo (bottom), each blown up to 1000 by 400 (the SVG four times its own size). The SVG's edges stay hard; the PNG's go soft
THE FIFTH TEST: an SVG carried from the Finder onto the timeline lands as a shelf tile would, on a graphics track from 0:01 for five seconds, the way Premiere takes a file dropped on a sequence
